case_linkage: No causal variant has been established by this literature module. BUB1B, CEP57 and TRIP13 are conditional mechanism branches, not findings in this participant. Add the locally reviewed Track 1 allele/transcript evidence before narrowing the branch. No measured gene-expression signature is available in this ledger; disease-gene lists and regulator enrichment must not be labeled measured up/down regulation.
submission_requirements: Submit a PDF or Markdown report explaining variant loss/gain of function, disrupted pathway, downstream consequence, and drug rationale; include the team/username in the filename.
Supply reproducible code and configuration in a GitHub repository; the repository must become public after the hackathon.
Supply a three-minute YouTube or Vimeo pitch video and identify one team submitter.
Track 2 uses expert qualitative review; only the latest entry is reviewed. The live official page currently permits three submissions per team.
Record the actual AI provider, plan/tier, and data-handling setting; do not infer account terms.

official_overview.title: Official Rare Disease, Real Kid MVA Hackathon overview
official_overview.supports: Track 2 seeks existing approved medications as follow-up hypotheses; three-submission limit.

track2_requirements.title: Official Track 2 submission requirements
track2_requirements.supports: Required report, variant mechanism, repository, video, AI disclosure and latest-entry review.

bubr1_mva.title: Molecular Causes for BUBR1 Dysfunction in the Human Cancer Predisposition Syndrome Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy (2010)
bubr1_mva.supports: Allele-dependent BUBR1 dysfunction in MVA; no drug efficacy inference.

cep57_mva.title: Snape et al. Mutations in CEP57 cause mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome (2011)
cep57_mva.supports: Biallelic CEP57 loss of function and centrosome/microtubule biology.

trip13_mva.title: Yost et al. Biallelic TRIP13 mutations predispose to Wilms tumor and chromosome missegregation (2017)
trip13_mva.supports: TRIP13 loss, spindle-checkpoint impairment and genetic rescue in patient-derived cells.

nac_replication.title: Slow Replication Fork Velocity of Homologous Recombination-Defective Cells Results from Endogenous Oxidative Stress (2016)
nac_replication.supports: NAC restored replication speed and reduced extra centrosomes in homologous-recombination-defective hamster cells; not an MVA model.

nac_cancer.title: Sayin et al. Antioxidants accelerate lung cancer progression in mice (2014)
nac_cancer.supports: NAC-associated tumor acceleration in oncogene-driven mouse lung models supplies counter-evidence, not a quantified MVA risk.

nac_fda.title: FDA ACETADOTE prescribing information, revised July 2025
nac_fda.supports: US acetylcysteine injection approval for acetaminophen-associated hepatic injury; hypersensitivity and fluid-overload warnings.

rapamycin_sasp.title: Laberge et al. MTOR regulates the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype by promoting IL1A translation (2015)
rapamycin_sasp.supports: Rapamycin suppressed SASP cytokines in experimentally senescent cells, not restoration of MVA chromosome segregation.

sirolimus_label.title: Pfizer RAPAMUNE US prescribing information
sirolimus_label.supports: US sirolimus indications include kidney-transplant rejection prophylaxis and lymphangioleiomyomatosis; immunosuppression and impaired wound-healing concerns.

colchicine_fda.title: FDA colchicine capsules prescribing information (2023)
colchicine_fda.supports: US approval for gout-flare prophylaxis; tubulin polymerization disruption and nonclinical aneuploidy via mitotic nondisjunction. Historical label establishes approval, not a comprehensive current safety review.

sirt2_bubr1.title: North et al. SIRT2 induces the checkpoint kinase BubR1 to increase lifespan (2014)
sirt2_bubr1.supports: SIRT2 stabilizes BubR1; NMN increased BubR1 abundance in mice. Lifespan evidence was from SIRT2 overexpression, not proof of NMN treatment efficacy in MVA.

mechanisms.description: Some pathogenic alleles impair the abundance or function of BUBR1, a spindle-checkpoint component. Establish whether the specific allele leaves functional residual protein before considering stabilization. Protein abundance alone is insufficient to show checkpoint rescue.
mechanisms.required_direction: Restore demonstrated checkpoint dysfunction; avoid weakening checkpoint activity or assuming every missense allele has the same effect.

mechanisms.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants can disrupt centrosomal functions associated with microtubule organization and chromosome-number maintenance. This branch must be experimentally distinguished from a primary checkpoint defect.
mechanisms.required_direction: Restore the affected centrosome/spindle function, not indiscriminate microtubule inhibition.

mechanisms.description: In reported patient-derived cells, biallelic loss of TRIP13 impaired the spindle assembly checkpoint and chromosome segregation; restoration of TRIP13 rescued these defects. Cancer-cell strategies that inhibit TRIP13 cannot be imported as rescue hypotheses for inherited loss of function.
mechanisms.required_direction: Recover the allele-specific checkpoint defect; do not infer desired inhibition from tumor overexpression studies.

candidates.name: Acetylcysteine (NAC)
candidates.mechanism_action: Redox modulation through a cysteine/glutathione-related mechanism; not replacement of a missing spindle-checkpoint protein.
candidates.rationale: A conditional cellular experiment could ask whether independently measured oxidative stress contributes to replication stress in the relevant MVA model. NAC improved replication-related phenotypes in homologous-recombination-defective hamster cells, a different disease mechanism. This evidence supports an assay hypothesis only.

approval.indication: Prevention or reduction of hepatic injury following potentially hepatotoxic acetaminophen ingestion

uncertainties: No MVA rescue or human MVA efficacy evidence is established in this ledger; oxidative stress in the relevant cells is unmeasured.
NAC accelerated progression in oncogene-driven lung-cancer mouse models. This counter-evidence matters when considering a cancer-predisposition syndrome, but cannot quantify risk in MVA.
Reduced stress markers could coexist with persistence or expansion of abnormal clones. Regulatory approval of an acute-use formulation does not establish suitability for chronic research translation.
The cited label includes serious hypersensitivity and fluid-overload warnings. Exposure, tissue penetration, formulation and interactions need independent review.

variant_mechanism.reason: Causal allele and downstream cellular consequence are unverified.

pathway_activation.reason: Measure oxidative stress and replication-fork phenotype first.

genome_safety.reason: Exclude abnormal-clone expansion and assess p53-associated responses.

exposure_feasibility.reason: No relevant tissue exposure or formulation bridge established.

validation.question: Does a redox-associated component of replication stress contribute causally to the cell phenotype?
validation.design: Compare variant-bearing cells, isogenic correction and matched control cells, with vehicle and an orthogonal redox perturbation; blind imaging and include independent biological replicates. An exposure-ranging laboratory design requires specialist review.
validation.readouts: Redox assays, DNA-fiber measures, viable-cell counts, live mitotic lineages, micronuclei, karyotype, checkpoint function, and longitudinal abnormal-clone abundance.
validation.falsification: Reject the hypothesis if target engagement fails, if stress changes without improved segregation, if apparent improvement is explained by killing/cytostasis, or if abnormal clones expand.

candidates.name: Sirolimus (rapamycin)
candidates.mechanism_action: Inhibits mTORC1; may modify a measured senescence-associated secretory phenotype rather than correct the causal segregation defect.
candidates.rationale: Rapamycin suppressed inflammatory secretion in experimentally senescent human cells. A relevance test is justified only if the case model independently shows an mTOR-linked secretory phenotype. Suppressing cytokines is not evidence of restored chromosome segregation or development.

approval.indication: Kidney-transplant organ-rejection prophylaxis and lymphangioleiomyomatosis, under the label's population restrictions

uncertainties: The primary evidence involves induced senescence, not MVA cells or patient treatment.
No mTOR activation or causal secretory phenotype is established in this case; enrichment of pathway genes would not establish either.
Immunosuppression, infection susceptibility, impaired wound healing, growth effects and exposure interactions complicate translation; existing approval does not solve these issues.
Cell-cycle slowing can create a misleading drop in mitotic-error counts; compare error frequency per completed division and track growth.

pathway_activation.reason: Measure mTOR activity and secretory phenotype independently.

genome_safety.reason: Exclude cytostasis artifacts, checkpoint bypass and abnormal-clone selection.

validation.question: Does mTOR-dependent secretion cause a reversible downstream phenotype?
validation.design: Use matched variant/corrected cultures and conditioned-medium transfer, with vehicle and an orthogonal mTOR perturbation. Include proliferation-matched controls and blind analysis.
validation.readouts: mTOR target engagement, cytokine secretion, conditioned-medium effects, viable-cell yield, division-normalized segregation errors and clonal karyotypes.
validation.falsification: Deprioritize if baseline pathway activation is absent, secretory changes do not improve function, or improvements disappear after controlling for proliferation; reject if genomic stability worsens.

candidates.name: Colchicine
candidates.mechanism_action: Disrupts microtubule polymerization; the FDA label describes induction of aneuploidy through mitotic nondisjunction.
candidates.rationale: An anti-inflammatory association or a shared pathway annotation cannot justify a chromosome-segregation rescue claim. Its documented mechanism opposes the proposed objective of preserving mitotic fidelity.
candidates.exclusion_reason: Exclude from disease-rescue shortlist because antimitotic action and labeled nonclinical aneuploidy provide a concrete mechanism conflict.
uncertainties: Rejection applies to the proposed MVA disease-rescue purpose, not to every approved use.
The historical label is sufficient to document the direction conflict; no claim of comprehensive current label review is made.

variant_mechanism.reason: The case allele is unverified, and no rescue mechanism is established.

genome_safety.reason: Regulatory nonclinical evidence describes aneuploidy through mitotic nondisjunction.

validation.question: Can the triage workflow identify an adverse mechanism despite shared pathway annotations?
validation.design: Use colchicine as a documentary negative control for direction-of-effect review, not a treatment candidate; inspect the regulatory mechanism and nonclinical evidence.
validation.readouts: Recorded tubulin effect, chromosome-segregation direction and exclusion reason.
validation.falsification: The triage workflow fails if an annotation overlap or hypothetical anti-inflammatory benefit overrides the documented antimitotic conflict.

candidates.name: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN; mechanistic comparator)
candidates.mechanism_action: NAD precursor studied in the SIRT2/BubR1 stability pathway; not interchangeable with nicotinamide, which inhibited sirtuins in the cited experiments.
candidates.rationale: The study increased BubR1 abundance with NMN in mice and extended lifespan through genetic SIRT2 overexpression. These are distinct experiments; neither demonstrates NMN efficacy in human MVA. A residual-functional-BUBR1 hypothesis would not generalize to absent protein, CEP57 loss or TRIP13 loss.

approval.formulation: No approved medicinal formulation established in this ledger
approval.indication: No approved drug indication established here; supplement availability is not evidence of medicinal approval

uncertainties: Retained as a mechanistic comparator, outside the approved-drug shortlist unless authoritative medicinal approval is verified.
More protein does not ensure that a mutant protein works. The implicated allele must retain relevant activity.
Do not substitute nicotinamide for NMN: the cited cell experiments found nicotinamide decreased BubR1 abundance.

variant_mechanism.reason: Requires a BUB1B-specific residual-protein mechanism, not merely an MVA label.

pathway_activation.reason: NAD/SIRT2 limitation is not demonstrated in the relevant cells.

functional_rescue.reason: No allele-specific checkpoint or segregation rescue measured.

genome_safety.reason: Need to exclude stabilization of nonfunctional protein and clonal adverse effects.

exposure_feasibility.reason: Drug approval and a clinically relevant exposure bridge remain unverified.

validation.question: Is residual functional BUBR1 destabilization reversible through SIRT2 in the relevant model?
validation.design: First measure allele-specific abundance and checkpoint function; compare genetic SIRT2 perturbation with isogenic correction and appropriate controls. Keep the NMN arm exploratory until approval status is verified.
validation.readouts: BUBR1 abundance/stability, SIRT2 engagement, checkpoint response, mitotic lineage errors and viable-cell karyotypes.
validation.falsification: Reject this branch if BUBR1 is absent or functionally irrecoverable, if abundance changes without checkpoint rescue, or if the causal gene belongs to a different mechanism.
